suggestions.description: The blocked source row truncates the explicit unavailable status, so its visible reason stops after the browser-verification wording and Kindle.
evidence: In all five 930x1240 source-manager captures with source B, the subtitle around x=100..287, y=746..762 is ellipsized before the unavailable clause. The gray source name, dashed warning tile and Uninstall action remain visible. This is a status-readability issue, not evidence that an unavailable operation is enabled or that a backend operation is blocked.

The case sidecars contain the full browser-verification/unavailable subtitle and available=false for source B. The issue is the visible projection of that truthful state, not the underlying state value.

HANDOFF.md section 5.4 requires a browser-verification-dependent source to show a concise verification/unavailable status and an Uninstall action. prototype/sc-sources.dc.html line 71 uses a concise status that retains the unavailable keyword; docs/DESIGN_HANDOFF.md requires blocked state to be explicit.
suggestions.recommendation: Shorten the source-manager blocked subtitle or reserve a visible unavailable status segment before optional detail. Keep the browser-verification reason and unavailable state readable within the existing 400-pixel installed column, while retaining the warning tile and Uninstall action. Recheck the five affected states on the same candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: Selected language chips and their single-result, dense-result and empty-result outcomes are visually covered. The PNGs do not independently establish the tap sequence, resetting to page one after changing language, or whether source membership is filtered correctly beyond the visible captured records. English language selection is outside this assigned batch.

The saved repository row and its removed/empty visible outcome are covered, and the supplied checks describe actual persisted records. Independent HTTP import, storage persistence after restart, Remove dispatch, Done and outside dismissal were not executed by this reviewer.

First/last folio labels, unavailable directional-action visibility, stable allocations and ten/four-row limits are covered. The batch does not show the open center jump grid or establish selection, outside dismissal, swipe behavior or repeated boundary-input clamping.

Visible artwork-only landscape output is covered. LTR input mapping, normal lower-right page turning, absence of an invisible footer-cycle hit zone, input generation fences, retained-scene wake, refresh timing and physical device behavior cannot be established from this single static PNG.

limitations: Exactly the eight assigned candidate PNGs were opened with tools.view_image. No other candidate, reference, processed-input, expected-oracle or difference image was loaded.

This supplemental batch has no independent reference PNG. Textual scope, relevant HANDOFF/prototype declarations and the supplied case metadata support the review; no exact pixel-match-to-reference claim is made.

Only existing JSON/text/PNG files and read-only SHA256 identity checks were used. No application, prototype runtime, build, test suite, smoke test or runtime probe was launched locally or remotely; no git operation or product modification was performed.

The existing mechanical_passed fields and sidecar checks were treated as supplied evidence rather than new verification results. Actual persistence, event dispatch and interaction behavior require the root review's independent remote evidence.

The captures identify the desktop backend and Scribe design profile at unit native scale. They do not qualify physical panel output, sensor behavior, hardware waveforms, sleep/wake behavior, touch-target response or a 512 MiB memory limit.
This is an eight-case supplemental result with one actionable finding, not a declaration that the complete round or applicable matrix is clean.
